messages:
Aritra M.: quick thread: re-followup on canary/ab fallback design. RFC landed some ideas but we need a compact emergency policy that runtime can evaluate in <500ms. thoughts?

Sofia L.: runtime currently has a tiny decision hook: if p99 > configured_ms -> fallback. Too blunt. We saw harmless transient spikes cause premature fallbacks last week.

Gary W.: Agree. We need a small stateful evaluator with hysteresis + sample thresh. Proposal: short window latency probe (30s) + medium window quality probe (5m), combine by max-normalized score.

Linh T.: Can you lay out the math?

Gary W.: simple: latency_score = clamp((p99_ms - target_ms) / target_ms, 0, 1) ; quality_score = clamp((baseline_eval - current_eval) / baseline_eval, 0, 1). hybrid_score = max(latency_score * w_l, quality_score * w_q). If hybrid_score > threshold and samples >= min_samples -> trigger.

Aritra M.: max() vs weighted sum? max() gives dominance to either signal which we may want (latency or quality alone should be able to trigger). weighted-sum is more conservative.

Sofia L.: operationally prefer dominance for emergency latency; quality regressions can be slower so maybe use weighted sum there. Suggest action: runtime can use dominance rule for immediate hedges and notify control-plane which runs weighted-sum for decisions that change rollout config.

ops-bot: telemetry: probe alert at 2026-02-23T09:12:04Z route=/chatgen p99=910ms target=400ms samples=180 eval_delta=+1.8%

Linh T.: important to enumerate allowed runtime actions. From low->high: "reduce-batch", "fallback-quantized", "route-to-baseline", "pause-canary". Each action should have a priority and minimum dwell time.

Gary W.: Also include an "inform-only" mode where runtime emits a decision_event but takes no action. Useful for early learning.

Aritra M.: policy schema fields we need: policy_id, strategy (dominance|weighted), weights (comma list), threshold, min_samples, latency_window_s, quality_window_s, actions (comma list), cool_down_s, recovery_samples. All strings.

Sofia L.: add "allowed_actions_per_tier" so hosted vs dedicated can have different capabilities.

Linh T.: tests: simulate 3 scenarios: latency-only spike, quality-only drift, combined. verify that runtime action + control-plane reconciliation behave as intended and no flip-flop within cool_down.

ops-bot: note: scheduled runbook task created: canary-sim-harness job queued, id=job-8812.

Gary W.: logging: the decision_event should include flattened fields: policy_id, route, score, latency_component, quality_component, samples, action_taken, decision_source (runtime/control-plane), decision_ts. easy JS/JSON parsing for postmortem.

Aritra M.: alerts: P0 if runtime performs route-to-baseline without prior control-plane inform (unexpected hard fallback), P1 for >3 soft-degrades in 30m on same route.

Sofia L.: rollout: let's start with default conservative policy: strategy=weighted, weights=latency:0.4,quality:0.6, threshold=0.75. On latency-sensitive routes override to dominance with latency priority.

Linh T.: who takes tasks? I'll draft schema PR for policy contract and a tiny mock evaluator lib for runtime. Gina (SRE) can own alerts mapping.

Aritra M.: sweet. action items: Linh -> schema PR by Tue EOD; Gary -> decision_event telemetry + sample payload by Thu; Sofia -> update RFC with dominance/weighted split and defaults by Fri; Linh + Gary -> add sim tests next week.

Sofia L.: one more note: preserve auditability. all runtime decisions should write an append-only event to control-plane for later correlation.

Aritra M.: thanks all. filing followup doc with examples after schema PR lands.

ops-bot: reminder: next architecture sync Thu 10:00am to review PRs.
